newsitem.title: USA: Mattel to issue refund for Cabbage Patch dolls.
newsitem.headline: Mattel to issue refund for Cabbage Patch dolls.

text.p: Toy maker Mattel Inc. said Monday it will stop making the Cabbage Patch Kids Snacktime Kids dolls and offer a $40 refund to owners following reports of children getting their hands and hair stuck in the doll's mouth.
Since the introduction of the dolls last fall, more than 500,000 dolls have been sold, making it one of the hottest items of the season.

A spokesman for the company said he did not know if Mattel would be forced to take a one-time charge against earnings to pay for the refund program because it was unclear how many of the dolls would be returned.
The dolls, a battery operated version of Cabbage Patch dolls that were a big hit in 1984, are designed to "eat" plastic french fries and other fake food and deposit it in the doll's backpack.
Recently, however, safety officials have received dozens of reports about the dolls chewing girls' hair or fingers.

Mattel said the refund followed reports of children getting their hair and fingers caught in the mouths of the dolls. The company said neither it nor the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission had identified a serious safety hazard associated with the dolls in testing.

"Nonetheless, we remain deeply concerned with the satisfaction of all our consumers and in maintaining their long-standing confidence in the safety and value of our toys," said Jill Barad, Mattel's chief executive officer. "Our job is to bring joy to children's lives. If any of our products are causing concerns, we are committed to responding in a responsible manner."
